content.content:
1	Many liquid handling installations add a small, accurately measured quantity of a concentrate to a much larger stream of a carrier liquid that is already flowing in a pipe. The concentrate may be aggressive, staining, strongly coloured, biologically active, or simply expensive, and the quantity that must be added is small in comparison with the carrier flow. The addition therefore has to be made repeatably, without measuring the concentrate by eye, and without allowing the concentrate to reach any part of the installation other than the carrier stream itself.
2	
3	Two practical difficulties dominate this kind of dosing. The first is separation of the two liquids upstream of the point of addition. A dosing device sits between a concentrate source and a pressurised carrier line, and any path that momentarily connects the two allows carrier liquid to be forced back into the concentrate source or allows concentrate to migrate into the carrier line at a time when no dose is called for. Devices that rely on separately actuated shut-off elements to keep the two sides apart depend on those elements being commanded in the correct order, so a control fault, a lost signal, or a slow-acting element can open both sides at once.
4	
5	The second difficulty is residue. The surfaces that the concentrate touches, in particular the port through which it enters the metering volume and the seat of the check element through which the dose leaves, retain a film of concentrate after the dose has been delivered. That film drips into the carrier stream between doses, so the quantity actually added is not the quantity that was measured. It also dries, crystallises, or reacts on the wetted surfaces, so that a valve which was accurate when new drifts, sticks, or seizes in service. The usual remedy is to break the valve out of the line and clean it by hand, which takes the installation out of service and exposes the person doing the work to the concentrate. Where a rinse is provided at all, it is commonly a separate operation that has to be commanded after the dose, and it therefore depends on an operator or a controller performing an extra step at the right moment.
6	
7	Dose selection presents a further difficulty. Adjustable dosing devices are often set by a screw or by an electronically stored value. A screw setting can be lost during cleaning and gives no indication of what was set. An electronic setting requires power, a sensor and a display at the valve, which is unwelcome in wet, washdown or hazardous locations, and it tells the operator only what the controller believes rather than what the mechanism will actually deliver.
8	
9	There remains a need for an inline metering valve in which the separation of the concentrate from the carrier liquid is enforced by the geometry of the moving parts rather than by the order in which external commands arrive, in which the surfaces wetted by the concentrate are rinsed by the carrier liquid as an unavoidable part of the return of the metering element, and in which the selected dose is both retained and displayed mechanically.
10

1	In the following description, the terms upstream and downstream refer to the direction of travel of the carrier liquid from the inlet toward the outlet, and the terms axial and radial refer to the axis along which the piston slides.
2	
3	FIG. 1 shows an inline liquid metering valve 10 having a cylindrical housing 12 with an inlet 14 at one axial end and an outlet 16 at the opposite axial end, a metering sleeve 18 fixed within the housing 12, a cartridge 64 retained in the housing 12 by a threaded end cap 66, and a transparent window 52 in the housing 12.
4	
5	The inline liquid metering valve 10 is connected in a line that already carries a flowing carrier liquid. Carrier liquid enters at the inlet 14, passes along the housing 12, and leaves at the outlet 16. That flow is the main flow into which each dose of concentrate is delivered, and it is also the flow that rinses the valve. The metering sleeve 18 is spaced radially inward from the inner surface of the housing 12 over part of its length.
6	
7	FIG. 2 shows the metering sleeve 18 defining a dose chamber 20, a concentrate port 22 opening into the dose chamber 20 and a carrier-liquid admission port 24 opening into the dose chamber 20. FIG. 2 further shows an upstream sealing land 30 and a downstream sealing land 32 joined by a reduced-diameter waist 34 in the fill position, and a one-way outlet valve 38.
8	
9	The dose chamber 20 is cylindrical. The concentrate port 22 is a radial port through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and is connected in use to a concentrate source. The carrier-liquid admission port 24 passes through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 at an axial position downstream of the concentrate port 22, and admits carrier liquid to the dose chamber 20. The metering sleeve 18 further defines a flush bypass 26 that opens downstream of the dose chamber 20.
10	
11	A piston 28 is axially slidable in the dose chamber 20 between a fill position and a discharge position. The upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 are axially spaced from one another on the piston 28 and are joined by the reduced-diameter waist 34. Each sealing land bears on the wall of the dose chamber 20, while the waist 34 stands clear of that wall. A piston rod 36 extends from the piston 28 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 and is arranged to be driven through a stroke and a return stroke. The one-way outlet valve 38 is arranged to pass liquid from the dose chamber 20 toward the outlet 16 and to prevent flow in the opposite direction.
12	
13	In the fill position the waist 34 connects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20, and the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolate the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. Concentrate accordingly passes from the concentrate source through the concentrate port 22 into the dose chamber 20 to form a measured volume of concentrate, the extent of which is fixed by the travel then permitted to the piston 28. Throughout the fill position the carrier-liquid path is closed to the concentrate, because the downstream sealing land 32 overlies the carrier-liquid admission port 24 while the upstream sealing land 30 closes the dose chamber 20 on the other side of the waist 34.
14	
15	Movement of the piston 28 toward the discharge position closes the concentrate port 22 before the downstream sealing land 32 uncovers the carrier-liquid admission port 24. The upstream sealing land 30 arrives at the concentrate port 22 and shuts it while the downstream sealing land 32 is still overlying the carrier-liquid admission port 24. Only after that has happened does continued travel of the piston 28 carry the downstream sealing land 32 clear of the carrier-liquid admission port 24. Carrier liquid then enters through the carrier-liquid admission port 24 behind the measured volume of concentrate in the dose chamber 20 and expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve 38 toward the outlet 16, where it joins the main flow.
16	
17	The axial ordering of the faces of the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 relative to the edges of the concentrate port 22 and the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is chosen so that the concentrate port 22 is closed at every position of the piston 28 at which the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is open. There is accordingly no position of the piston 28 at which the concentrate source communicates directly with the carrier-liquid path. The separation of the two liquids is a property of the geometry of the piston 28 and the metering sleeve 18. It does not depend on the order in which external commands are given, on any control signal, or on the correct operation of a separately actuated shut-off element. A slow stroke, an interrupted stroke, or a stroke reversed part way through cannot open both ports at once, because the port that must close does so at an earlier point on the same continuous path of travel than the point at which the other port opens.
18	
19	FIG. 3 shows the piston 28 during the return stroke toward the fill position, with a flexible lip 56, the follower pin 44 holding a flush poppet 58 open, an annular rinse channel 60, two radial rinse openings 62 of which one is directed across the concentrate port 22, and the flush bypass 26.
20	
21	The flexible lip 56 is carried on the upstream sealing land 30 and bears on the wall of the dose chamber 20. As the return stroke begins, the flexible lip 56 wipes the wall of the dose chamber 20.
22	
23	The annular rinse channel 60 lies between an outer surface of the metering sleeve 18 and an inner surface of the housing 12, and is supplied with carrier liquid from the inlet 14. The two radial rinse openings 62 pass through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and connect the annular rinse channel 60 to the dose chamber 20. One of the two radial rinse openings 62 is directed across the concentrate port 22 and the other is directed across the one-way outlet valve 38.
24	
25	The flush poppet 58 is normally closed and is connected to the flush bypass 26. Near the end of the return stroke, the follower pin 44 reaches the flush poppet 58 and opens it. Carrier liquid then flows from the inlet 14 through the annular rinse channel 60, through the two radial rinse openings 62 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 to the outlet 16. The rinse liquid therefore reaches the outlet 16, as the dose does, and is carried away in the main flow.
26	
27	The flush poppet 58 closes before the waist 34 reconnects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20. The concentrate port 22 is closed throughout the interval in which the annular rinse channel 60 communicates with the flush bypass 26. Only when the flush poppet 58 has closed does the continuing return of the piston 28 bring the waist 34 back into register with the concentrate port 22, at which point the dose chamber 20 is charged again for the next dose.
28	
29	Because the follower pin 44 that opens the flush poppet 58 is carried by the piston rod 36, the rinse occurs once for every dose and at the same point in every cycle. It is not a separate operation, it needs no command, and it cannot be omitted while the valve continues to be used. In the following description, the terms upstream and downstream refer to the direction of travel of the carrier liquid from the inlet toward the outlet, and the terms axial and radial refer to the axis along which the piston slides.

FIG. 1 shows an inline liquid metering valve 10 having a cylindrical housing 12 with an inlet 14 at one axial end and an outlet 16 at the opposite axial end, a metering sleeve 18 fixed within the housing 12, a cartridge 64 retained in the housing 12 by a threaded end cap 66, and a transparent window 52 in the housing 12.

The inline liquid metering valve 10 is connected in a line that already carries a flowing carrier liquid. Carrier liquid enters at the inlet 14, passes along the housing 12, and leaves at the outlet 16. That flow is the main flow into which each dose of concentrate is delivered, and it is also the flow that rinses the valve. The metering sleeve 18 is spaced radially inward from the inner surface of the housing 12 over part of its length.

FIG. 2 shows the metering sleeve 18 defining a dose chamber 20, a concentrate port 22 opening into the dose chamber 20 and a carrier-liquid admission port 24 opening into the dose chamber 20. FIG. 2 further shows an upstream sealing land 30 and a downstream sealing land 32 joined by a reduced-diameter waist 34 in the fill position, and a one-way outlet valve 38.

The dose chamber 20 is cylindrical. The concentrate port 22 is a radial port through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and is connected in use to a concentrate source. The carrier-liquid admission port 24 passes through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 at an axial position downstream of the concentrate port 22, and admits carrier liquid to the dose chamber 20. The metering sleeve 18 further defines a flush bypass 26 that opens downstream of the dose chamber 20.

A piston 28 is axially slidable in the dose chamber 20 between a fill position and a discharge position. The upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 are axially spaced from one another on the piston 28 and are joined by the reduced-diameter waist 34. Each sealing land bears on the wall of the dose chamber 20, while the waist 34 stands clear of that wall. A piston rod 36 extends from the piston 28 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 and is arranged to be driven through a stroke and a return stroke. The one-way outlet valve 38 is arranged to pass liquid from the dose chamber 20 toward the outlet 16 and to prevent flow in the opposite direction.

In the fill position the waist 34 connects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20, and the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolate the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. Concentrate accordingly passes from the concentrate source through the concentrate port 22 into the dose chamber 20 to form a measured volume of concentrate, the extent of which is fixed by the travel then permitted to the piston 28. Throughout the fill position the carrier-liquid path is closed to the concentrate, because the downstream sealing land 32 overlies the carrier-liquid admission port 24 while the upstream sealing land 30 closes the dose chamber 20 on the other side of the waist 34.

Movement of the piston 28 toward the discharge position closes the concentrate port 22 before the downstream sealing land 32 uncovers the carrier-liquid admission port 24. The upstream sealing land 30 arrives at the concentrate port 22 and shuts it while the downstream sealing land 32 is still overlying the carrier-liquid admission port 24. Only after that has happened does continued travel of the piston 28 carry the downstream sealing land 32 clear of the carrier-liquid admission port 24. Carrier liquid then enters through the carrier-liquid admission port 24 behind the measured volume of concentrate in the dose chamber 20 and expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve 38 toward the outlet 16, where it joins the main flow.

The axial ordering of the faces of the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 relative to the edges of the concentrate port 22 and the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is chosen so that the concentrate port 22 is closed at every position of the piston 28 at which the carrier-liquid admission port 24 is open. There is accordingly no position of the piston 28 at which the concentrate source communicates directly with the carrier-liquid path. The separation of the two liquids is a property of the geometry of the piston 28 and the metering sleeve 18. It does not depend on the order in which external commands are given, on any control signal, or on the correct operation of a separately actuated shut-off element. A slow stroke, an interrupted stroke, or a stroke reversed part way through cannot open both ports at once, because the port that must close does so at an earlier point on the same continuous path of travel than the point at which the other port opens.

FIG. 3 shows the piston 28 during the return stroke toward the fill position, with a flexible lip 56, the follower pin 44 holding a flush poppet 58 open, an annular rinse channel 60, two radial rinse openings 62 of which one is directed across the concentrate port 22, and the flush bypass 26.

The flexible lip 56 is carried on the upstream sealing land 30 and bears on the wall of the dose chamber 20. As the return stroke begins, the flexible lip 56 wipes the wall of the dose chamber 20.

The annular rinse channel 60 lies between an outer surface of the metering sleeve 18 and an inner surface of the housing 12, and is supplied with carrier liquid from the inlet 14. The two radial rinse openings 62 pass through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and connect the annular rinse channel 60 to the dose chamber 20. One of the two radial rinse openings 62 is directed across the concentrate port 22 and the other is directed across the one-way outlet valve 38.

The flush poppet 58 is normally closed and is connected to the flush bypass 26. Near the end of the return stroke, the follower pin 44 reaches the flush poppet 58 and opens it. Carrier liquid then flows from the inlet 14 through the annular rinse channel 60, through the two radial rinse openings 62 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 to the outlet 16. The rinse liquid therefore reaches the outlet 16, as the dose does, and is carried away in the main flow.

The flush poppet 58 closes before the waist 34 reconnects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20. The concentrate port 22 is closed throughout the interval in which the annular rinse channel 60 communicates with the flush bypass 26. Only when the flush poppet 58 has closed does the continuing return of the piston 28 bring the waist 34 back into register with the concentrate port 22, at which point the dose chamber 20 is charged again for the next dose.

Because the follower pin 44 that opens the flush poppet 58 is carried by the piston rod 36, the rinse occurs once for every dose and at the same point in every cycle. It is not a separate operation, it needs no command, and it cannot be omitted while the valve continues to be used. The rinse also occurs while the concentrate port 22 is shut and after the wall of the dose chamber 20 has been wiped.

FIG. 4 shows an index collar 40 having a helical cam groove 42 engaged by a follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36, three selectable axial stop faces 46, a spring-biased detent 48 engaging one of three detent recesses 50, and three dose setting numerals 54.

The index collar 40 surrounds the metering sleeve 18. Each full stroke of the piston 28 draws the follower pin 44 along the helical cam groove 42 and turns the index collar 40 by one increment, so that the index collar 40 advances by itself as the valve is used and needs no separate indexing drive.

The three axial stop faces 46 are carried by the index collar 40 at different axial positions. The stop face presented by the current increment of rotation limits the travel of the piston 28 and thereby sets the dose volume, so that the three axial stop faces 46 correspond to three dose volumes. The spring-biased detent 48 engages one of the three detent recesses 50 to retain the selected setting until the index collar 40 is next indexed.

The transparent window 52 in the housing 12 shows one of the three dose setting numerals 54 carried by the index collar 40. The dose setting numeral presented at the transparent window 52 is the one associated with the axial stop face then limiting the travel of the piston 28, so that the dose setting is mechanically visible without electronics. What is seen at the transparent window 52 is the position of the index collar 40 itself.

The cartridge 64 contains the piston 28, the metering sleeve 18, the one-way outlet valve 38 and the flush poppet 58, and is removable from the housing 12 as a unit. Removing the threaded end cap 66 withdraws the cartridge 64 from the housing 12 along the axis of the dose chamber 20 without disturbing the connections at the inlet 14 and the outlet 16, so that the cartridge 64 is replaced as a unit while the housing 12 remains in the line.

In use, carrier liquid flows through the housing 12 from the inlet 14 to the outlet 16. With the piston 28 in the fill position, concentrate is admitted through the concentrate port 22 and past the waist 34 into the dose chamber 20 to form a measured volume, the upstream sealing land 30 and the downstream sealing land 32 isolating the carrier-liquid admission port 24 from the concentrate port 22. The piston 28 is then advanced toward the discharge position so as to close the concentrate port 22 and thereafter to uncover the carrier-liquid admission port 24 with the downstream sealing land 32. Carrier liquid is admitted through the carrier-liquid admission port 24 behind the measured volume and expels the measured volume through the one-way outlet valve 38 toward the outlet 16. The extent of the travel available to the piston 28, and therefore the measured volume, is fixed by the selected one of the three axial stop faces 46.

The piston 28 is then returned toward the fill position. During the return, the flexible lip 56 on the upstream sealing land 30 wipes the wall of the dose chamber 20, and the follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36 opens the normally closed flush poppet 58. Carrier liquid flows through the annular rinse channel 60 between the metering sleeve 18 and the housing 12, through the two radial rinse openings 62 in the metering sleeve 18 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 that opens downstream of the dose chamber 20 to the outlet 16. The flush poppet 58 is closed before the waist 34 reconnects the concentrate port 22 to the dose chamber 20. Over the same full stroke, the follower pin 44 travelling in the helical cam groove 42 turns the index collar 40 by one increment, the spring-biased detent 48 enters the next of the three detent recesses 50, and the dose setting numeral then presented at the transparent window 52 shows the setting that will govern the next dose. The valve is thereby left charged, rinsed and set, ready for the following cycle.

The foregoing description sets out embodiments of the invention. A skilled reader may make changes of detail to the described embodiments without departing from the scope of the claims that follow.

input.summary: Source ledger: I traced every limitation of claims 1-20, all 29 reference numerals, and every structural, positional, flow-path and operational statement in draft/04 through draft/10 and figures/fig-01..04 to the inventor text. The disclosure and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md are identical, and they affirmatively support: the cylindrical housing with inlet and outlet at opposite axial ends (10/12/14/16); the fixed metering sleeve 18 defining cylindrical dose chamber 20, radial concentrate port 22, carrier-liquid admission port 24 and flush bypass 26 opening downstream; piston 28 with upstream land 30, downstream land 32 and reduced-diameter waist 34; the fill-position isolation, the close-before-uncover ordering, carrier liquid entering behind the measured volume, one-way outlet valve 38, and the "ordering of the port edges and lands" no-communication property; piston rod 36 with follower pin 44; index collar 40 with helical cam groove 42, one-increment-per-full-stroke indexing, three selectable axial stop faces 46, spring-biased detent 48 with three recesses 50, transparent window 52 and three collar-carried numerals 54; flexible lip 56 on the upstream land wiping first; normally closed flush poppet 58 opened by the follower pin near the end of the return stroke; annular rinse channel 60 between sleeve and housing; two radial rinse openings 62 directed across the concentrate port and the one-way outlet valve; poppet closing before the waist reconnects the concentrate port; cartridge 64 containing piston, sleeve, outlet valve and poppet, retained by threaded end cap 66 and withdrawable without disturbing the housing connections; and the requested apparatus plus method claim classes. Dependent claims 2-12 and 14-20 each map to an express disclosure sentence; claims 4/16 and 5 are direct restatements of the disclosed ordering and the "poppet closes before the waist reconnects" timing. The renaming of the inventor's "three reference numerals" to "three dose setting numerals 54" is a disambiguation, not a substantive change, and the brief's preserved terminology (metering sleeve, dose chamber, flush bypass, index collar, flush poppet, annular rinse channel) is used throughout. Cross-reference and government-support sections match brief.md ("Not applicable."), the title matches the working title, and no means-plus-function language appears. I found no untraced limitation, no untraced numbered part, and no unsupported optional embodiment: every figure-brief element that is not expressly disclosed (ball-and-seat form of valve 38, conical head/stem form of poppet 58, ball-and-coil form of detent 48, the concentrate-source tube, window placement, numerals drawn as blank patches) is expressly labelled "shown schematically" in the brief only, and the claims, Brief Description and detailed description all remain shape-neutral. No "by way of example", "any closed outline", or similar shape-justifying sentence leaked into the application text. Numeral hygiene is clean: all 29 numerals in numerals.md appear in exactly one part meaning each, the per-figure numeral sets in draft/07 and draft/08 match the "Numerals on this sheet" lists in the four briefs exactly, numeral 44 denotes the same follower pin in both FIG. 3 and FIG. 4, and no numeral is orphaned or reused. No named/lettered section line exists anywhere (FIG. 1 is a plain longitudinal section and FIGS. 2-3 are enlargements of it), so there is no section-line designation to reconcile across resulting view, source-view brief and drawing description. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any file. The abstract is a single paragraph of about 145 words and tracks the claim-1 subject matter. Three internal-consistency defects remain, none of them a source-fidelity gap: (1) FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 place the same follower pin 44 on opposite sides of the metering sleeve's left end, so the pin cannot both bear on the poppet stem and sit in the cam groove as drawn; (2) FIG. 3 puts the left radial rinse opening 62 at the same axial station as the upstream sealing land that the same brief says covers the concentrate port, so the depicted rinse jet has no path to the surface it is said to sweep; and (3) the detailed description introduces "the follower pin 44" with a definite article before its own antecedent. Prior-art characterizations in draft/05 were not traced to inventor text, as instructed; a later review traces them to prior_art/.

findings.title: FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 place follower pin 44 on opposite sides of the metering sleeve's left end
findings.where: figures/fig-03.md (Geometry, 4th bullet) and figures/fig-04.md (Geometry, 1st and 3rd bullets)
findings.detail: The two briefs assign mutually exclusive axial stations to the same numbered part 44. FIG. 3 puts the pin on the portion of the piston rod that lies beyond (left of) the metering sleeve's left end. FIG. 4 puts the pin inside the axial extent of the index collar, and it also states that the sleeve ("an unnumbered tube") projects leftward beyond the collar's left end, which places the collar, and therefore the pin, to the right of the sleeve's left end. Because the disclosure requires the pin to remain engaged in the cam groove at all times ("a helical cam groove engaged by a follower pin carried by the piston rod", "Each full piston stroke turns the index collar by one increment") while also opening the poppet near the end of the return stroke, the two depicted positions cannot both be correct for the same pin. This is a drawing-level inconsistency about a claimed element (claim 1 "a piston rod extending from the piston and carrying a follower pin"; claim 6 "a helical cam groove engaged by the follower pin"), not a source gap.
findings.evidence: fig-03.md: "A plain shaft extends leftward on the axis past the sleeve's left end, and a short pin projects upward from it, bearing on the poppet stem and holding the head off its seat." fig-04.md: "It surrounds an unnumbered tube, a short length visible beyond the collar's left end." and "A piston rod is drawn as a plain horizontal shaft entering the view from the left on the collar axis and ending within the left part of the collar surface. A short follower pin projects radially from the end of the shaft, its outer end sitting within the narrow band of the groove."
findings.fix: In figures/fig-04.md, replace the first Geometry bullet's clause "It surrounds an unnumbered tube, a short length visible beyond the collar's left end." with "It surrounds an unnumbered tube whose left end lies within the collar, the collar extending leftward beyond that end." This puts the collar's left region, and hence the follower pin engaged in the groove, at the same axial station as the pin shown in FIG. 3, and leaves every other bullet and every target unchanged.

findings.title: FIG. 3 places the left radial rinse opening 62 at the axial station the same brief says is covered by the upstream sealing land
findings.where: figures/fig-03.md (Geometry, bullets beginning "An opening through the upper sleeve band, covered by the left portion" and "Two openings through the lower sleeve band")
findings.detail: The brief states that the concentrate port is covered by the left (upstream) piston land in the depicted return-stroke position, and in the next bullet places the left radial rinse opening directly beneath that same port and aimed at it. A land that covers the port's inner mouth also occupies the bore at the station of the opening beneath it, so the depicted rinse jet is blocked by the land and has no path either to the port mouth or onward to the flush bypass at the right. The result contradicts the description's stated flush flow path. The underlying timing ("The flush poppet closes before the waist reconnects the concentrate port") comes from the disclosure and should not be changed; only the drawn axial station of the left rinse opening needs to be clear of the lands.
findings.evidence: fig-03.md: "An opening through the upper sleeve band, covered by the left portion, is the concentrate port, with a tube rising from it across the gap and outer band." and "Two openings through the lower sleeve band connect the rinse channel to the bore: the radial rinse openings. The left lies beneath the concentrate port, aimed at it". draft/08-detailed-description.md: "Carrier liquid then flows from the inlet 14 through the annular rinse channel 60, through the two radial rinse openings 62 across the concentrate port 22 and the one-way outlet valve 38, and through the flush bypass 26 to the outlet 16."
findings.fix: In figures/fig-03.md, replace "The left lies beneath the concentrate port, aimed at it; the right at a ball on a conical seat, shown schematically in a passage rising through the upper band." with "The left lies just right of the right portion of the piston, clear of both piston portions, and is aimed up and left toward the concentrate port; the right lies at a ball on a conical seat, shown schematically in a passage rising through the upper band." Target 62 continues to read "the left lower opening".

findings.title: Detailed description introduces "the follower pin 44" with a definite article before its antecedent
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "FIG. 3 shows the piston 28 during the return stroke" (first occurrence of numeral 44), compared with the later FIG. 4 paragraph
findings.detail: Numeral 44 is first used in the FIG. 3 paragraph with a definite article, but the element is not introduced until the FIG. 4 paragraph, where it is introduced afresh with an indefinite article. Every other numbered part in the description is introduced with an indefinite article at first mention and referred to definitely thereafter, so this is an isolated antecedent-basis slip that should be corrected before filing.
findings.evidence: First mention: "FIG. 3 shows the piston 28 during the return stroke toward the fill position, with a flexible lip 56, the follower pin 44 holding a flush poppet 58 open ..." Later mention: "FIG. 4 shows an index collar 40 having a helical cam groove 42 engaged by a follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36 ..."
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md, change the FIG. 3 paragraph to read "... with a flexible lip 56, a follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36 and holding a flush poppet 58 open ...", and in the FIG. 4 paragraph change "engaged by a follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36" to "engaged by the follower pin 44 carried by the piston rod 36".

structured_output.summary: Source ledger: I traced every limitation of claims 1-20, all 29 reference numerals, and every structural, positional, flow-path and operational statement in draft/04 through draft/10 and figures/fig-01..04 to the inventor text. The disclosure and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md are identical, and they affirmatively support: the cylindrical housing with inlet and outlet at opposite axial ends (10/12/14/16); the fixed metering sleeve 18 defining cylindrical dose chamber 20, radial concentrate port 22, carrier-liquid admission port 24 and flush bypass 26 opening downstream; piston 28 with upstream land 30, downstream land 32 and reduced-diameter waist 34; the fill-position isolation, the close-before-uncover ordering, carrier liquid entering behind the measured volume, one-way outlet valve 38, and the "ordering of the port edges and lands" no-communication property; piston rod 36 with follower pin 44; index collar 40 with helical cam groove 42, one-increment-per-full-stroke indexing, three selectable axial stop faces 46, spring-biased detent 48 with three recesses 50, transparent window 52 and three collar-carried numerals 54; flexible lip 56 on the upstream land wiping first; normally closed flush poppet 58 opened by the follower pin near the end of the return stroke; annular rinse channel 60 between sleeve and housing; two radial rinse openings 62 directed across the concentrate port and the one-way outlet valve; poppet closing before the waist reconnects the concentrate port; cartridge 64 containing piston, sleeve, outlet valve and poppet, retained by threaded end cap 66 and withdrawable without disturbing the housing connections; and the requested apparatus plus method claim classes. Dependent claims 2-12 and 14-20 each map to an express disclosure sentence; claims 4/16 and 5 are direct restatements of the disclosed ordering and the "poppet closes before the waist reconnects" timing. The renaming of the inventor's "three reference numerals" to "three dose setting numerals 54" is a disambiguation, not a substantive change, and the brief's preserved terminology (metering sleeve, dose chamber, flush bypass, index collar, flush poppet, annular rinse channel) is used throughout. Cross-reference and government-support sections match brief.md ("Not applicable."), the title matches the working title, and no means-plus-function language appears. I found no untraced limitation, no untraced numbered part, and no unsupported optional embodiment: every figure-brief element that is not expressly disclosed (ball-and-seat form of valve 38, conical head/stem form of poppet 58, ball-and-coil form of detent 48, the concentrate-source tube, window placement, numerals drawn as blank patches) is expressly labelled "shown schematically" in the brief only, and the claims, Brief Description and detailed description all remain shape-neutral. No "by way of example", "any closed outline", or similar shape-justifying sentence leaked into the application text. Numeral hygiene is clean: all 29 numerals in numerals.md appear in exactly one part meaning each, the per-figure numeral sets in draft/07 and draft/08 match the "Numerals on this sheet" lists in the four briefs exactly, numeral 44 denotes the same follower pin in both FIG. 3 and FIG. 4, and no numeral is orphaned or reused. No named/lettered section line exists anywhere (FIG. 1 is a plain longitudinal section and FIGS. 2-3 are enlargements of it), so there is no section-line designation to reconcile across resulting view, source-view brief and drawing description. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any file. The abstract is a single paragraph of about 145 words and tracks the claim-1 subject matter. Three internal-consistency defects remain, none of them a source-fidelity gap: (1) FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 place the same follower pin 44 on opposite sides of the metering sleeve's left end, so the pin cannot both bear on the poppet stem and sit in the cam groove as drawn; (2) FIG. 3 puts the left radial rinse opening 62 at the same axial station as the upstream sealing land that the same brief says covers the concentrate port, so the depicted rinse jet has no path to the surface it is said to sweep; and (3) the detailed description introduces "the follower pin 44" with a definite article before its own antecedent. Prior-art characterizations in draft/05 were not traced to inventor text, as instructed; a later review traces them to prior_art/.

findings.title: FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 place follower pin 44 on opposite sides of the metering sleeve's left end
findings.where: figures/fig-03.md (Geometry, 4th bullet) and figures/fig-04.md (Geometry, 1st and 3rd bullets)
findings.detail: The two briefs assign mutually exclusive axial stations to the same numbered part 44. FIG. 3 puts the pin on the portion of the piston rod that lies beyond (left of) the metering sleeve's left end. FIG. 4 puts the pin inside the axial extent of the index collar, and it also states that the sleeve ("an unnumbered tube") projects leftward beyond the collar's left end, which places the collar, and therefore the pin, to the right of the sleeve's left end. Because the disclosure requires the pin to remain engaged in the cam groove at all times ("a helical cam groove engaged by a follower pin carried by the piston rod", "Each full piston stroke turns the index collar by one increment") while also opening the poppet near the end of the return stroke, the two depicted positions cannot both be correct for the same pin. This is a drawing-level inconsistency about a claimed element (claim 1 "a piston rod extending from the piston and carrying a follower pin"; claim 6 "a helical cam groove engaged by the follower pin"), not a source gap.
findings.evidence: fig-03.md: "A plain shaft extends leftward on the axis past the sleeve's left end, and a short pin projects upward from it, bearing on the poppet stem and holding the head off its seat." fig-04.md: "It surrounds an unnumbered tube, a short length visible beyond the collar's left end." and "A piston rod is drawn as a plain horizontal shaft entering the view from the left on the collar axis and ending within the left part of the collar surface. A short follower pin projects radially from the end of the shaft, its outer end sitting within the narrow band of the groove."
findings.fix: In figures/fig-04.md, replace the first Geometry bullet's clause "It surrounds an unnumbered tube, a short length visible beyond the collar's left end." with "It surrounds an unnumbered tube whose left end lies within the collar, the collar extending leftward beyond that end." This puts the collar's left region, and hence the follower pin engaged in the groove, at the same axial station as the pin shown in FIG. 3, and leaves every other bullet and every target unchanged.

findings.title: FIG. 3 places the left radial rinse opening 62 at the axial station the same brief says is covered by the upstream sealing land
findings.where: figures/fig-03.md (Geometry, bullets beginning "An opening through the upper sleeve band, covered by the left portion" and "Two openings through the lower sleeve band")
findings.detail: The brief states that the concentrate port is covered by the left (upstream) piston land in the depicted return-stroke position, and in the next bullet places the left radial rinse opening directly beneath that same port and aimed at it. The result contradicts the description's stated flush flow path. The underlying timing ("The flush poppet closes before the waist reconnects the concentrate port") comes from the disclosure and should not be changed; only the drawn axial station of the left rinse opening needs to be clear of the lands.
